name: authoring
description: Author and audit what an AI harness reads: SKILL.md files, shell scripts, help text, command names.
skillInstructions:
Kimi Code tool mapping for the authoring skills.

The authoritative mapping is owned by the sibling repo dEitY719/harness-skills at `references/kimi-tools.md` (dotfiles #1410 F-5). Read it there when a skill names a tool you do not recognise; this repo deliberately keeps no copy. Summary:

- "Ask the user" -> `AskUserQuestion`. `authoring:skill-refactor` (plan confirmation before any write), `authoring:command-rename` (ambiguous command family, mapping design), and `authoring:ux-guidelines` (target selection) all wait on a real answer.
- `TodoWrite` -> Kimi Code's `TodoList` tool.
- "Dispatch a subagent" -> `Agent` with `subagent_type: "coder"` (implementation) or `"explore"` (read-only). Never pass `general-purpose`. `authoring:skill-create` fans out `agents/{grader,comparator,analyzer}.md` and `authoring:command-rename` delegates issue creation.
- Read / Write / Edit / Bash / Grep / Glob keep their exposed Kimi names. Search contents with `Grep`; match paths with `Glob`.
- `authoring:skill-check` and `authoring:sh-check` are read-only audits: never call `Write`, `Edit`, or a mutating `Bash` command from them. They report every criterion, including failures, instead of stopping at the first one.
- `authoring:skill-create` ships Python helpers under `skills/skill-create/scripts/` and `eval-viewer/`. They are plain `python3` entry points; run them through `Bash`. Skip the eval loop rather than faking its output when the harness cannot spawn probe sessions.
- `authoring:command-rename` never renames anything. It only reads the repo and files GitHub issues through `gh` via `Bash`; the rename itself runs later from that issue.

interface.shortDescription: Author and audit skills, scripts, and command names
interface.longDescription: Authoring bundles the six skills that keep an agent harness's own source material in shape: skill-create, skill-check, skill-refactor, sh-check, ux-guidelines, and command-rename.
